newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis on alert for Islamic Jihad attack.
newsitem.headline: Israelis on alert for Islamic Jihad attack.

text.p: Israel went on high alert on Sunday for fear of a possible suicide attack by Palestinian militants of Islamic Jihad marking the one-year anniversary of their leader's assassination.

"It's in context of the possibility of Islamic Jihad committing an attack to mark a year since the death of Fathi Shqaqi, the organisation's leader, and security forces take this threat very seriously and so this preparedness," Police Chief Assaf Hefetz told army radio.
Islamic Jihad, responsible for a series of suicide attacks in Israel, accuses the Jewish state of killing Shqaqi, who was gunned down on October 26, 1995, in Malta. His assassins were never caught.
"We don't know the kind of attack exactly but it could be an explosion, suicide, shots," Hefetz said.
Police set up roadblocks throughout Israel on Sunday, causing traffic snarls on some of Israeli's busiest highways at morning rush hour.
Security sources said a car bomb might already have been smuggled into Israel and its operators could be waiting for a green light to carry out the attack.

"We estimate there is some sort of an infrastructure of terrorists which is ready for an attack, and our activities are reducing and stalling them," Hefetz told Israel Radio when asked the chances a guerrilla was already inside Israel.
Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani told army radio the expected target was in one of the Israeli cities -- Jerusalem, Tel Aviv or Haifa.

Palestinian police in the self-ruled Gaza Strip last month arrested dozens of Islamic Jihad members before the Shqaqi anniversary to pre-empt any attacks by the movement, a PLO security official said.

Islamic Jihad and Hamas leaders have been in jail since suicide bombings in February and March, responsibility for which was claimed by Hamas, the other leading Islamic resistance group in Palestinian areas.
Israel on October 23 sealed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, barring Palestinians from going to work in the Jewish state, for fear of guerrilla attacks. That closure remains in place.
In the West Bank city of Hebron, Jewish settlers hurled petrol bombs at a Palestinian house, setting it ablaze and injuring five people, one critically, family members said.

Under an interim peace deal, Hebron was to be handed over to the PLO last March, but was delayed for security reasons. PLO and Israeli officials have failed to reach agreement on the handover of the city, a flashpoint of violence where about 400 settlers live in the heart of more than 100,000 Palestinians.
